body:
Does saving a QOA file using `ResourceSaver.save()` actually write a standard `.qoa` file that external audio players will accept? As I understand it, `ResourceSaver.save()` always writes Godot-specific formats with its own headers, even if the data is encoded in a standard format (e.g. lossy Texture2D which uses WebP). This is done because the headers contain metadata for how the file should be read, which standard formats generally can't store (or not consistently across formats).

As I understand it, FileAccess cannot write the QOA file unless you manually reimplement the header writing, then write the packed data after it. It is technically possible to do, but directing users to FileAccess when they basically have to reimplement format saving themselves may be misleading (especially if they were expecting a one-liner).

If it's not possible to save a `.qoa` file from Godot with only a few lines of code, I would just not mention it in the error message.

Unlike IMA ADPCM, the QOA implementation within Godot actually creates full QOA file data including the header, therefore the following should be valid:
```gdscript
var f := FileAccess.open("path/to/file.qoa", FileAccess.WRITE)
    f.store_buffer(my_qoa_audiostream.data)
```

Here is the moment the header is encoded:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/97241ffea6df579347653a8ce0c75db44e28f0c8/scene/resources/audio_stream_wav.h#L279
